description: Golden pricing/tax/combo/Route-44 dataset for issue #9 (tests/conformance). Ported from app/backend/tests/test_order_state.py, test_tool_calling.py, and test_combo_orders.py so both the S1-3 conformance scenarios and a future C# backend (S4) assert against the exact same cent-accurate cases. MONEY CONTRACT (PR #38 review item 1): line = unit * qty * (happyHourDiscount iff isDrink and happy hour is active); subtotal = sum(line); tax = subtotal * taxRate, computed ONCE per order (never per line, never re-derived from a rounded subtotal); finalTotal = subtotal + tax. There is NO rounding at any step of this arithmetic -- '.2f'/currency formatting is presentation-only and must never feed back into subtotal/tax/finalTotal math. Every money value below (unitPrice/price/taxRate/happyHourDiscount/expectedSubtotal/expectedTax/expectedFinalTotal/expectedTotal) is stored as a quoted, exact decimal string -- computed with true decimal arithmetic, not IEEE-754 double -- specifically so it can be loaded as C# `decimal` (see GoldenOrderPricingData.cs) without ever round-tripping through `double`. The live Python backend still computes in double internally and so will echo back tiny float noise (e.g. 0.8151999999999999 instead of 0.8152) on the wire; scenarios parse that wire value directly into `decimal` via `JsonElement.GetDecimal()` (never `GetDouble()`) and compare with an absolute tolerance of 0.000001m, which absorbs exactly that double noise while still failing a genuinely wrong implementation (e.g. one that rounds tax to cents per line before summing).

happyHourBoundaryInstants.note: order_state.py's is_happy_hour() only compares now().hour (start <= hour < end); minutes/seconds are irrelevant. The first four instants use the same date as the pre-existing FixedClockConformanceFixture (2026-07-04, CDT/-05:00); the last two are a winter (CST/-06:00) instant pair added per PR #38 review item 5 specifically to catch a hardcoded -05:00/UTC-offset bug that the summer-only cases can't -- America/Chicago is -06:00 in January, not -05:00.

reset_order must zero the combo absorption slot counters, not just the line items: a fully-satisfied combo followed by reset_order followed by a fresh bare combo of the same kind must show as incomplete again (test_order_state.py::reset_order absorbed_sides/absorbed_drinks reset; PR #38 review item 4, Rick's M1 -- a mutation that removes the absorbed-counter reset from reset_order must fail this)

N5 (PR #38 re-review should-fix 4): two combos need two side slots total; Tots quantity 2 in a single call exactly fills both slots (order_state.py's per-call `to_absorb = min(quantity, slots_available)` then `session['absorbed_sides'] += to_absorb`), leaving nothing standalone for Tots; Onion Rings x1 then finds zero side slots remaining and is charged in full as its own line. A mutation that increments absorbed_sides by a flat 1 per call instead of by to_absorb would under-count the two-unit Tots absorption as only one slot filled, letting Onion Rings wrongly absorb into the still-apparently-open second slot -- collapsing this to 1 line item at 16.98 instead of 2 at 20.87.

PR #99 decision 1 (Rick's review): French Toast Sticks Combo's bundle.slots is ["drinks"] only, so Tots added afterward is NOT absorbed and is charged in full -- the bug the old name-based ('combo' in item name) engine had, which wrongly gave every '...Combo'-named item a free side slot too (app/backend/menu_utils.py::bundle_slots, order_state.py post-bundle-absorption block)
PR #99 decision 1: French Toast Sticks Combo absorbs its one drink slot for free and is then complete with no side required (app/backend/menu_utils.py::bundle_slots)
PR #99 decision 1: Crispy Tenders Dinner - 3 piece's bundle.slots is ["drinks"] only, same as French Toast Sticks Combo -- absorbs a drink for free but a side stays a full-price standalone line

PR #99 decision 1: Corn Dog Wacky Pack®'s bundle.slots is ["sides","drinks"] (same as a regular Combo) even though its name doesn't contain the word 'combo' -- the old name-based engine gave it zero slots and never absorbed anything for it

PR #99 decision 1: $6 All-American Smasher™ Meal's bundle.slots is ["sides","drinks"] despite not containing the word 'combo' in its name -- absorbs one side and one drink for free, same as a regular Combo

PR #99 decision 1: two different breakfast bundles with different slot shapes track side/drink capacity independently: French Toast Sticks Combo (drinks-only) contributes 0 side capacity, Bacon Breakfast Burrito Combo contributes 1 side + 1 drink, so total capacity is 1 side + 2 drinks; a mutation that shares one flat 'combo_count' across both bundles instead of per-component bundle_slots() capacity would wrongly report this complete before the second drink is added

spokenTotalCases.description: PR #38 second re-review should-fix 2 (active, non-half-cent): reuses taxCases' 'Drink + non-drink, no happy hour' case. #104: Cherry Limeade re-based from artificial 2.99 to its real medium menu price 2.89, so finalTotal is now 9.2556, rounding unambiguously to $9.26 under EITHER rounding convention (round-half-away-from-zero or IEEE round-half-to-even). This stays an active assertion against the live Python backend and still catches Rick's N2 (spoken text built from the pre-tax subtotal instead of finalTotal) today: a backend speaking the pre-tax total would say $8.57, not $9.26.

PR #38 second re-review should-fix 2 (Skip'd, lands exactly on a half cent, #46): a whole-cent subtotal can never land finalTotal (subtotal * 1.08) exactly on a half cent -- 8n mod 100 = 50 has no integer solution since gcd(8,100)=4 does not divide 50 -- so this case needs a subtotal with 3+ decimal places, which only arises here from a happy-hour-halved odd-cent drink price. #104: re-based to real menu prices while preserving the exact half-cent arithmetic -- Cherry Limeade Route 44 3.79 (its real route44 price) halved to 1.895 (happy hour) + Salted Caramel Toffee Croissant Bites 1.99 (its real price) x2 (3.98) => subtotal 5.875, tax 0.47 (exact), finalTotal 6.345. #46 fixes this: exact Decimal math with ROUND_HALF_UP renders 6.345 as $6.35 (half cent rounds up), matching the round-half-away-from-zero display rule (C# `decimal` + `MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero`) used to compute expectedSpokenTotalText below.

Rick's N21 (#46): trailing-zero cents must still render two decimal places, not truncate to '$32.4'. #104: re-based from the artificial Tots@10.00 (now a real 2.79) to the real '$6 All-American Smasher™ Meal' price (5 x $6.00, no happy hour): subtotal 30.00, tax 2.40, finalTotal 32.40.

Rick's N21 (#46): a non-midpoint value whose third decimal digit forces a round-up, distinct from the exact-half-cent case above. Tots medium x3 @2.79, no happy hour: subtotal 8.37, tax 0.6696 (8.37 * 0.08), finalTotal 9.0396 -- rounds up to $9.04 (not a ceiling: this is a genuine round-half-up-style carry from the thousandths digit, not merely truncating/ceiling every fractional cent).
